description: Date of the early parliamentary election being forecast.
source: Balkan Insight 2026-09-09 (decree 9 Sep 2026); ODIHR EOM page

description: Number of MPs elected.
source: Law on Election of MPs Art.3; ODIHR NAM report 2026-07-30 p.8

description: Whole country is one electoral unit.
Seats needed for a majority: floor(seats_total/2)+1.
Ordinary participation threshold.

Base of the 3% test. Art.81 says 3% of the votes "of the total number of voters who voted". Art.74/85 list "voters who voted" separately from used ballots and valid ballots, which maps to dataset column voters_turned_out. HOW THE RIK APPLIES IT IN PRACTICE WAS NOT VERIFIED; the pipeline runs all three.
source: Law Art.74,81,85 (2020 consolidated text); RIK and CRTA explainers

description: Quotients of national-minority lists are multiplied by 1.35 in the largest-quotient calculation.
source: Law Art.81(2); RIK and CRTA explainers

description: Statutory wording uplifts the quotients of ALL minority lists; official explainers describe the uplift for minority lists under 3%. Outcomes differ only if a minority list reaches 3%.
Equal quotients on the last seat: more total votes wins.
If no list reaches 3%, all lists with votes take part.
Minority status is decided by the RIK per list at proclamation; May 2026 amendments specify the criteria. It is an INPUT (cfg_list_registry_2026), never inferred from votes.
Voters in the register for 25 Oct 2026, as reported from the RIK decision.
Register size given to ODIHR NAM by the Ministry in July 2026. Information only.
USER-SPECIFIED participating voters, lower end. Scenario assumption, not a verified prediction.
USER-SPECIFIED participating voters, upper end. Scenario assumption, not a verified prediction.

Municipal 2026 registers are NOT in the data (only the national total). Each 2023 unit register is scaled by register_total_2026 / 2023 national register. Sensitivity: the 13 sample municipalities show a larger register decline than the national ratio, so unit-level drift is uncertain.

Abroad (33000) and institutions (55001) are held at 2023 attendance in turnout calibration. Reports suggest diaspora registration for 2026 is far higher than 2023 attendance abroad (unverified); replace once RIK special-register data are loaded.
territories.region_id values whose 2023 turnout RATE is held fixed in calibration (RS23 = Kosovo i Metohija: displaced-voter registers, 2023 turnout 3-33%).
A municipality has a recent local election if it was held at most this many months before the target date. Sensitivity run required.
source: Analyst choice (not a legal or empirical quantity)

description: election_id prefix identifying national parliamentary elections in the package.
National elections with turnout, list votes and mandates needed to claim a meaningful backtest.
Tolerance for vote shares summing to 1.
Master seed for stochastic steps (spawned per component).
Denominator list for the log-ratio coordinates (any list works; results are invariant to the choice).
Lists modelled from polls (log-ratio to the reference). Lists polled in too few polls are still included; their posterior is then prior-dominated and flagged.
All reported shares are treated as shares of decided voters (log-ratios are insensitive to the base as long as it is common across lists within a poll).
source: Analyst choice; base is stated for only two of five polls

description: Variance inflation for sampling error of quota/clustered surveys. Sensitivity 1.0-4.0.
Sample size used ONLY where the source does not state it (variance is not otherwise inflated for that).
Lower bound for the SD of pollster effects on the log-ratio scale. The pipeline uses max(this, between-house SD of the loaded polls).
Daily SD of real opinion movement on the log-ratio scale (about 0.024 over 35 days).
SD of a polling miss shared by all houses on election day (log-ratio scale). Not estimated: no past poll-vs-result pairs are in the dataset. Sensitivity 0.05-0.20.
Prior SD of log-ratio levels (very weak).
Median combined share of non-minority lists that no poll reports separately (their share is carved out before the polled lists are scaled).
source: Analyst prior; the Faktor plus 16-20 Sep poll leaves 3.0 percent for all lists it does not name, minority lists included

description: Log-SD of that combined share.
Multiplier on the unit-level turnout dispersion estimated from the 2022-2023 change in valid votes (a lower bound for a longer interval).
Number of national-turnout grid points used to map participating voters to ballots and valid ballots (linear interpolation) in the national draws.
Dirichlet concentration (equal means) for splitting the combined share of the non-minority lists no poll reports separately among those lists.
List keys the coalition tokens @all_except_incumbent and the incumbent-anchored assumption set refer to.
List key the token @all_except_student and the student-anchored assumption set refer to.

ext_events types that can trigger the event-scenario mixture when dated AFTER the last poll (polls cannot have captured them). Departures, joinings, endorsements and measured shifts remain distinct types.
Unit-level log-weight SD used for pseudo-origins and families without a stable 2022-2023 swing estimate.
Upper bound on any estimated swing SD (families with few or tiny observations give unstable values).
Outcome column of s4_local_swing_panel used for the descriptive local summary and the alpha scenarios. Rows with a missing value are left out, not imputed.
Shifts (in participating voters) applied to BOTH ends of the user-specified turnout range to build alternative turnout scenarios. Scenario definitions, not forecasts of turnout.
Alternative design effects for the poll sampling error.
Alternative SDs of the shared election-day polling miss.
Multipliers on unit and region swing dispersion for the municipal layer (the backtest finds regional heterogeneity of roughly 0.3x to 2x).
Non-minority lists whose poll strength is swept to show how the seat outcome reacts around the 3 percent threshold.
Additive shifts of log(list / reference) used in the threshold sweep.
Draws per grid point in the threshold sweep.
Lists marked as minority lists in cfg_list_registry_2026 whose status is flipped to non-minority in a sensitivity run (the RIK decides; the group of this list is not stated in the sources).
Units whose expected valid votes fall below this are flagged in municipal outputs: their shares rest on a handful of votes (for example the polling-station units of region RS23).
Fixed values of the minority turnout responsiveness phi used in minority-outcome scenarios (0 = minority votes unchanged by turnout, 1 = proportional to valid votes).
Alternative mean shares of a group pool captured by new-entrant minority lists.
Upper bound on the number of dated re-estimations in the forecast timeline.
Distribution of national participating voters within the user-specified range.
Scales the unit baseline invalid-ballot rate (1 = unchanged).
Multiplier on unit-level swing dispersion estimated from 2022-2023.
Multiplier on regional swing dispersion estimated from 2022-2023 (5 regions: weakly identified).
Scenario grid for how much of a municipality local-election swing of the governing-coalition lists carries into its parliamentary geography (NOT identified).
SD of an unidentified mobilization effect of having held a recent local election (log scale, student-list geography). Mean 0 because no effect is identified.
Lower bound of phi: elasticity of a minority group vote to the change in valid votes (0 = unchanged, 1 = proportional).
Upper bound of phi (uniform draw).
Log-SD of a shock common to all lists of a minority group.
Mean share of an existing minority-group pool captured by a new entrant list of the same group.
Beta concentration for the capture share.
Median votes of a minority list with no historical analog and no group pool in the data (prior-only).
Log-SD for prior-only minority lists.
Monte Carlo draws for the national forecast.
Draws for which the municipal-level downscaling is run (municipal intervals).
Central interval levels reported.
Prediction-market prices are validation signals only and never enter the vote-share model.
